title: Unique Paths
description:
An m-by-n rectangular grid has a traveler at its upper-left cell. Count the routes to the lower-right cell when each move goes exactly one cell right or one cell down. There are no obstacles and routes are distinguished by their sequences of moves.

A cell can be reached only from the cell above it or from the cell to its left, so its route count is the sum of those two counts. A single cell has one route, consisting of zero moves.

Example 1:

Input: m = 3, n = 7
Output: 28

Choose the positions of two down moves among eight total moves: 28 routes.

Example 2:

Input: m = 3, n = 2
Output: 3

The down move can occur in any of three positions.

Example 3:

Input: m = 1, n = 1
Output: 1

Start and destination coincide, yielding one zero-move route.

Constraints:

  • 1 <= m, n <= 20
  • The number of routes fits a signed 64-bit integer.
